comment: The REST contract the access gateway serves (FIRECRAWL_PI_SPEC.md §16.1): the routes, the options each accepts, the limits and the evidence that covers them. services/access validates every request against it and services/access/client.mjs builds its URLs from it; scripts/m3/route-shapes.mjs checks each route's upstream shape against the pinned source.

mcp.comment: The MCP surface (FIRECRAWL_PI_SPEC.md §16.3, §17): the access gateway serves `path` after its own Host, Origin, token and body checks and proxies it to services/mcp, which registers one tool per entry below, its input schema generated from the named route's body in this manifest, and calls that route on the gateway with the caller's own token. A tool the spec names whose route is not enabled is listed under `omitted` by that route, whose not_enabled reason is the reason; since M5 none is.

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.title: Scrape a page
tools.description: Fetch one public web page through the private Firecrawl platform and return its content in the requested formats. Waits for the page (up to 110 s). Links to a fragment of the page itself (footnote markers, back-references, a table of contents) come back as their text, and every other link as written. A result larger than the tool payload limit comes back as a marked excerpt with the sizes of what was cut. A screenshot, and each screenshot action, comes back as the address of an artifact only your token can read, and neither is combined with the json format in one call; maxAge (milliseconds) serves your own cached answer when it is younger than that; proxy enhanced asks for the budgeted enhanced provider alone.

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.title: Map a site's URLs
tools.description: Discover the URLs of a public site from its sitemap and the links on its start page, without scraping each page. The start page is fetched like a scrape (it needs the scrape scope, keeps this call's timeout, and takes the residential route only when the home connection is blocked); fcpi.sources says how many links each source gave, and fcpi.pageError why the page gave none. A site with no sitemap yields its start page's links, and a crawl discovers the pages beyond them.

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.title: Search the web
tools.description: Search the web through the platform's private SearXNG and return the results' URLs, titles and snippets; with scrapeOptions.formats, each result page is scraped too. A search whose engines all failed, or whose backend is down, is an error naming the failure, never an empty list; a partial result says which engines did not answer.

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.title: Start a crawl
tools.description: Start a crawl of a public site. Returns the job id as soon as the job is durably recorded; the crawl runs in the background. Poll it with firecrawl_check_crawl_status. Every start carries an idempotency key, yours or one made for it and returned in the answer: to retry, call again with the same arguments and that key, and the same job comes back instead of a second one.

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status
tools.title: Read a crawl
tools.description: Read a crawl's status and one bounded page of its documents. When more documents remain, the answer holds nextSkip: call again with skip set to it. fcpi.state is the job's own state (RUNNING until it is archived, even when status already says completed); a finished crawl's fcpi gives its outcome: state (PARTIAL when some pages failed), failed, failures grouped by class with a detail, sample URLs and retryAt when they may be retried, and notes about the record itself. creditsUsed is left out when the core counts none. The id survives restarts of the MCP service and of the gateway.

tools.name: firecrawl_cancel_crawl
tools.title: Cancel a crawl
tools.description: Cancel a crawl: no new pages are dispatched and its state becomes cancelled. Cancelling a cancelled crawl succeeds again; a finished crawl cannot be cancelled.

tools.name: firecrawl_batch_scrape
tools.title: Start a batch scrape
tools.description: Start scraping a list of public URLs as one background job. Returns the job id as soon as it is durably recorded; poll it with firecrawl_batch_status. Every start carries an idempotency key, yours or one made for it and returned in the answer: to retry, call again with the same arguments and that key.

tools.name: firecrawl_cancel_batch
tools.title: Cancel a batch scrape
tools.description: Cancel a batch scrape: no new pages are dispatched and its state becomes cancelled. Cancelling a cancelled batch succeeds again; a finished batch cannot be cancelled. A platform extension, like the batch tools.

tools.name: firecrawl_batch_status
tools.title: Read a batch scrape
tools.description: Read a batch scrape's status and one bounded page of its documents. When more documents remain, the answer holds nextSkip: call again with skip set to it. fcpi.state is the job's own state (RUNNING until it is archived, even when status already says completed); a finished batch's fcpi gives its outcome: state (PARTIAL when some pages failed), failed, failures grouped by class with a detail, sample URLs and retryAt when they may be retried, and notes about the record itself. creditsUsed is left out when the core counts none.

tools.name: firecrawl_extract
tools.title: Extract structured data
tools.description: Extract data matching a JSON schema from up to ten given URLs, as one background job: each page is scraped, then read by the platform's budgeted model. Returns the job id once it is durably recorded; poll it with firecrawl_extract_status. Values a page does not hold come back null, never invented. Every start carries an idempotency key, yours or one made for it: to retry, call again with the same arguments and that key.

tools.name: firecrawl_extract_status
tools.title: Read an extraction
tools.description: Read an extraction job: its status and, once finished, the extracted data, the source URLs of each value, and any page or unit that failed and why.

tools.name: firecrawl_get_result
tools.title: Read a job's receipt
tools.description: Read the durable receipt of a crawl, batch or extraction job: its state and transitions, counts, error summary, retention and the address of its results.

tools.name: firecrawl_capabilities
tools.title: Describe this deployment
tools.description: Describe what this deployment supports: its routes, formats and limits, the core's and the job ledger's health, and the MCP tools it omits and why.
